🐛 Describe the bug
This might be ok-ish if all code is compiled, but for eager code in the graph module this may break. Similar to #112072

  
    
      pytorch/torch/csrc/dynamo/guards.cpp
    
    
         Line 434
      in
      63c089b
    
  
  
    

        
          
           struct GlobalStateGuard { 
        
    
  


Solutions
This needs to be guarded.
Notes

unlike: grad mode, which is

guarded
an in-graph mutation that needs to be turned into a side-effect


the situation here is reversed - ambient autocast is

not guarded
in-graph autocast ctx is at least in theory guaranteed to be localized to the graph (exits within the lifetime of the graph)



May be part of the root cause for #112164
This is particularly problematic for FSDP because there is autocast-dependent eager code in FSDP hooks to my understanding (to make decisions about activation/gradient comm dtype/compression).
Additional Details
That any in-graph autocast exits within the lifetime of the graph should be verified:

enforce that autocast manager always exits within the traced graph, or
we need to handle side-effects as we intend to do for set_grad_enabled (as there is a mutating API - set_autocast_enabled etc)

Repro
weights = torch.randn(10, 10, device="cuda")

def mod(x):
    return torch.mm(x, weights)

opt_inductor = torch.compile(mod, backend="inductor")
opt_eager = torch.compile(mod, backend="eager")
x = torch.randn(1, 10, device="cuda")

with torch.autocast('cuda', torch.float16):
    ref = mod(x)
    res = opt_inductor(x)
    res_eager = opt_eager(x)

print(ref.dtype, res.dtype, res_eager.dtype)  # float16, float16, float16

with torch.autocast('cuda', torch.bfloat16):  # No recompilation
    ref = mod(x)
    res = opt_inductor(x)
    res_eager = opt_eager(x)

print(ref.dtype, res.dtype, res_eager.dtype)  # bfloat16, float16, bfloat16

🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
Gradient clipping is a popular technique to scale gradients and avoid exploding gradients issues in RNNs/very deep networks. PyTorch offers a util torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_value_ that enables users to clip gradients such that they collectively have a capped maximum value.
While the torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_value_ should work, it is not ideal to have different apis (torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_value_ vs self.clip_grad_norm_) when handling the same feature. In that sense, adding clip_grad_value_ could contribute to a clearer
Call self._lazy_init to ensure stream synchronization is done appropriately
Apply inplace clamp on all gradients
Ensure that this works with nested FSDP instances as well.
That would also help for clearer design over distributed training tools built over PyTorch.
Alternatives
Use clip_grad_value_ from torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_value_ and self.clip_grad_norm_ when handling gradient norms on FSDP.

import torch

def f(x):
    y = x.clone()
    torch.set_grad_enabled(False)
    return y.clone()

f_compiled = torch.compile(f, backend='aot_eager', fullgraph=True)

print(torch.is_grad_enabled())
torch.set_grad_enabled(True)
y = f_compiled(x)

🐛 Describe the bug
import torch

class T(torch.Tensor):
    def __new__(cls, elem):
        return torch.Tensor._make_wrapper_subclass(cls, elem.shape, dtype=elem.dtype)

    def __init__(self, elem):
        self.elem = elem

    @classmethod
    def __torch_dispatch__(cls, func, types, args, kwargs=None):
        if func is torch.ops.aten.detach.default:
            (self,) = args
            return cls(torch.ops.aten.detach.default(self.elem))
        raise NotImplementedError(f"{func}")
    
x = torch.randn(3)
y = T(torch.randn(3))
    
print("ok")
with torch.inference_mode():
    x.detach()
    
print("fail")
with torch.inference_mode():
    y.detach()

this fails with
(/home/ezyang/local/a/pytorch-env) [ezyang@devgpu005.nha1 ~/local/a/pytorch (63a99720)]$ python no.py
ok
fail
Traceback (most recent call last):

    y.detach()
  File "/data/users/ezyang/a/pytorch/torch/_tensor.py", line 1397, in __torch_function__
    ret = func(*args, **kwargs)
RuntimeError: Cannot set version_counter for inference tensor

You can work around it with
    @classmethod
    def __torch_dispatch__(cls, func, types, args, kwargs=None):
        if func is torch.ops.aten.detach.default:
            (self,) = args
            with torch.inference_mode(False):  # NEW!
                return cls(torch.ops.aten.detach.default(self.elem))
        raise NotImplementedError(f"{func}")

suggesting that the proximal cause of the problem is that when we construct T inside the torch dispatch function, it is created as an inference mode tensor, even though the semantics of detach() on a non-inference mode tensor when inference mode is enabled is to create a non-inference tensor.
Not entirely sure what the correct fix is.

🐛 Describe the bug
Identical code for computing the l1 distance gives different values on CPU and MPS. MPS results don't have a diagonal zero matrix either:
import torch

# Set a deterministic seed
torch.manual_seed(42)

# Ensure MPS backend is available
if not torch.backends.mps.is_available():
    raise ValueError("MPS backend is not available on this machine.")

# Create a random tensor
A = torch.randn(9, 360000)

# Define the pairwise L1 distance function
def compute_l1_distances(tensor):
    N = tensor.shape[0]
    l1_distances = torch.empty(N, N)
    for i in range(N):
        l1_distances[i] = torch.sum(torch.abs(tensor[i] - tensor), dim=1)
    return l1_distances

# Compute on CPU
A_cpu = A.cpu()
l1_cpu = compute_l1_distances(A_cpu)
print("L1 distances (CPU):")

A_mps = A.to(torch.device("mps"))
l1_mps = compute_l1_distances(A_mps)
print("\nL1 distances (MPS):")
print(l1_mps)

# Check for differences
diff = (l1_cpu.cpu() - l1_mps.cpu()).abs().max().item()
print(f"\nMaximum absolute difference: {diff}")
